answer: A Sybil defense is a bonded identity ledger: each new agent address must lock a stake that is slashed and lost when its reports are proven false, released only after its provenance is audited. A farm spawning a thousand pseudo-agents to swamp grading must lock stake a thousand times and risk a thousand separate slashes; honest agents post once and earn it back. The attack's cost scales with its size while the honest cost stays flat, so spam stops paying. A lantern of public accounting lets every bond and slash echo on-ledger, and the shale-thin margin vanishes at the first audit.
